citation.title: Susceptibility of large populations of coupled oscillators

how_reached: journals.aps.org returns HTTP 403; the abstract was reached through PubMed (PMID 25679699). Full text not read.
why_this_source: This record exists to stop a conflation. There are two Daido susceptibilities thirty years apart. This is the FIELD-response one, it is the reference Hong et al. cite for gamma_sus = 1, and it does NOT carry the 1/4-vs-1 asymmetry.
observable: FIELD RESPONSE. How phase order responds to a synchronizing periodic force from outside.
frequency_class: Not a frequency-class paper. Its 'nonrandom' / 'most random' axis is about the INTERACTIONS (uniform K vs random J_ij), not about the frequencies.

quotes.quote: Susceptibility of large populations of coupled oscillators.
quotes.bears_on: The reference Hong et al. cite for gamma_sus = gamma'_sus = 1 is a separate, later Daido paper about response to an external force.

quotes.quote: the susceptibility diverges at the critical point in the nonrandom case with Widom's equality satisfied, while it exhibits a cusp in the most random case
quotes.bears_on: Widom's equality with beta = 1/2 and delta = 3 gives gamma = 1, which is consistent with the gamma_sus = 1 Hong et al. attribute to this paper — but the value itself was not read here.

numbers: NOT EXTRACTED. No exponent value was read from this paper; only the abstract was reached.
caveats: Do NOT read 'nonrandom case' / 'most random case' as regular vs random FREQUENCIES. Misreading it that way is a direct route to a confident and wrong published claim.
A citation to 'Daido's susceptibility exponent' with no year is ambiguous between two different physical objects.
